top.headline: Short delivery stride (49% of height; typical 70–87%)
top.title: Find your stride

metrics.label: Back-foot to front-foot contact
metrics.note: A foot contact was estimated (no clear foot-strike in this clip, or moved to keep the delivery order). Drag the event marker to the exact frame, or confirm it in the 'At this frame' card, to measure this.
metrics.explain: Duration of the delivery stride. Reported ± one frame (17 ms for this footage).

metrics.label: Front-foot contact to release
metrics.explain: How quickly you go from landing to letting the ball go. Shorter (with a stable front leg) usually means better energy transfer.

metrics.label: Elbow extension (UAH → release)
metrics.note: Elbow extension needs 120–240 fps slow motion (this clip has ~60 distinct fps); it isn't estimated from this video. Never a substitute for an accredited ICC test.
metrics.ref: ICC Illegal Bowling Regulations; Ferdinands & Kersting 2005; King & Yeadon 2013
metrics.explain: Straightening of the bowling elbow between the arm passing horizontal and release, computed the ICC way (maximum flexion minus the following minimum). A single camera cannot replace an accredited ICC test — use this only as a screening estimate.

metrics.label: Front knee at release
metrics.norm: Aim for 160° or straighter at release. Elite men average 167 ± 19°; a straighter front knee goes with faster bowling (r ≈ 0.4)
metrics.explain: A straighter front leg at release acts as a lever and is associated with higher ball speed; some flexion is normal and may reduce load.

metrics.label: Front knee bend after landing
metrics.norm: Elite men flex 9 ± 11° after FFC (guide range)
metrics.explain: Flexion of the front knee from landing to its most bent point. Together with the extension to release it gives the front-leg technique (Portus et al. 2004).

metrics.label: Back knee at back-foot contact
metrics.note: A foot contact was estimated (no clear foot-strike in this clip, or moved to keep the delivery order). Drag the event marker to the exact frame, or confirm it in the 'At this frame' card, to measure this.
metrics.norm: Injured bowlers 146° vs uninjured 156° at BFC (rear hip/knee)
metrics.explain: A very flexed back leg at back-foot contact was one of the strongest predictors of lumbar stress injury in a prospective elite study.

metrics.label: Trunk forward flexion at release
metrics.norm: Elite men ~42 ± 5° forward at release (guide range)
metrics.explain: How far the trunk is pitched towards the batter at release. Fast bowlers flex strongly through the delivery stride. This is the lean at the moment of release; 'Trunk flexion FFC → release' is how much it bends during the stride.

metrics.label: Trunk flexion FFC → release
metrics.norm: Elite men flex the trunk 31 ± 8° from FFC to release
metrics.explain: Trunk flexion produced during the delivery stride — a key contributor to ball speed.

metrics.label: Trunk side-bend at release
metrics.note: Not measurable from this camera view — film behind the bowler or front-on to measure it.
metrics.norm: Later-injured juniors 50 ± 6° vs uninjured 40 ± 8° (thorax lateral flexion at BR)
metrics.ref: Bayne et al. 2016; contested in elite adults (Alway 2021)
metrics.explain: Lateral flexion of the trunk away from the bowling arm. Large side-bend loads the lower back; it is one of the better single-camera measures from behind the bowler.

metrics.label: Shoulder alignment at back-foot contact
metrics.note: Not measurable from this camera view — film behind the bowler or front-on to measure it.

metrics.label: Hip-shoulder separation at BFC
metrics.note: Not measurable from this camera view — film behind the bowler or front-on to measure it.
metrics.norm: >= 30° at BFC classifies a mixed action
metrics.explain: Misalignment between hips and shoulders when the back foot lands; large values define a 'mixed' action, which twists the lower back.

metrics.label: Shoulder counter-rotation
metrics.note: Not measurable from this camera view — film behind the bowler or front-on to measure it.
metrics.norm: >= 30° is the common mixed-action criterion (stronger evidence in juniors)
metrics.explain: How much the shoulders rotate back towards side-on after back-foot contact.

metrics.label: Release height
metrics.norm: Elite men 113 ± 4% of standing height (guide range)
metrics.explain: Height of the ball at release as a percentage of your height (~1.96 m for a stature of 1.80 m). Single-camera precision is about ± 8 points.

metrics.label: Arm slot at release
metrics.note: Not measurable from this camera view — film behind the bowler or front-on to measure it.
metrics.norm: Angle of the bowling arm from vertical at release (descriptive; higher slot often costs more side-bend)
metrics.explain: 0° = bowling arm straight up (high arm); larger = more round-arm.

metrics.label: Delivery stride length
metrics.norm: Elite men 79 ± 7% of standing height (guide range)
metrics.explain: Distance between the ankles at front-foot contact.

priorities.headline: Short delivery stride (49% of height; typical 70–87%)
priorities.why: Distance between the ankles at front-foot contact.

drill.title: Find your stride
drill.cue: Push off and reach your front foot a little further down the pitch.
drills: Stride markers: mark a target front-foot position at ~75–80% of your height from the back foot (3 × 6).
Bound and stick: bound into the delivery stride and hold balance for two seconds (2 × 8).

strengths: Strong, braced front leg at release
Good forward bend of the upper body from landing to release
capture_tips: Filmed at 60 fps, so release timing is approximate: the arm moves about 33° from one frame to the next. Film in slow motion (120–240 fps) next time for precise release and elbow measurements.
Filmed side-on: knee, trunk flexion, stride and release height are measured well; add a clip from behind the bowler for side-bend and alignment.
coaching.disclaimer: Estimates from a single video. Not a medical assessment and not an ICC legality test.
